overview.description: Design and optimise proteins in silico before you ever touch a bench. Structure predictors (AlphaFold2, ESMFold) fold a sequence; generative models (RFdiffusion) invent new backbones; inverse-folding models (ProteinMPNN) choose sequences that fold to a target shape. You filter computationally, then order genes and validate.
objectives: predict a structure from sequence with AlphaFold2/ESMFold
generate a de novo backbone or binder with RFdiffusion
design sequences for a fold with ProteinMPNN (inverse folding)
rank designs in silico and plan experimental validation

steps.description: A design-build-test loop that starts on a GPU: specify the function, model or generate the structure, choose sequences, filter, then express and assay the winners.
steps.intro: Modern protein design front-loads the expensive wet-lab step with cheap in-silico screening: generate thousands of candidates, keep the few most likely to fold and function, and only build those.

instructions.title: Define the target
instructions.description: State the function: a binder to a target, an enzyme scaffold, a stabilised variant. Fix the constraints (interface, active site, size).

instructions.title: Model or generate
instructions.description: Fold candidate sequences with AlphaFold2/ESMFold, or generate new backbones toward the target with RFdiffusion.

instructions.title: Design sequences
instructions.description: Run ProteinMPNN on the backbone to pick sequences likely to fold to it; re-predict to check self-consistency (design then fold then compare RMSD).

instructions.title: Filter & order
instructions.description: Rank by pLDDT/ipTM, interface metrics, and self-consistency; order the top genes and clone into an expression vector.

instructions.title: Build & test
instructions.description: Express, purify (His-tag), and assay binding/activity/stability. Feed results back into the next design round.

submission.description: Design one protein (a binder, scaffold, or stabilised variant), show the in-silico evidence it should fold (structure prediction + self-consistency), and outline how you would express and test it.
